correctness.rationale: For every positive a,b,c, the line-graph odd-neighborhood parity equations imply x_uv=1+p_u+p_v, where p is uniquely recoverable from selected degrees. The full necessary-and-sufficient part equations (1+r_i)p_v=r_i+sum_{j≠i}t_j yield four disjoint parity classes and unique labelled representations. Selected edges split into two induced line-graph components by endpoint parity, establishing connectedness exactly. Complete weight sums count independent choices of constrained odd subsets. The minimum degree and exponential count for K_(1,2m,2m) follow algebraically. Independent finite C++ direct subsets and Python exact Gaussian elimination reproduce all test cases. Finite checks are not treated as an all-order proof.

originality.rationale: Caro–Klostermeyer establish foundational odd domination, and Caro–Klostermeyer–Yuster examine its connected variant, but their complete-multipartite host results do not establish the line-graph parity classification. Full primary result text for the triangular and rook line-graph families was examined and treats bases with respectively one homogeneous and two independent vertex classes, not three nonempty tripartite classes. The new four-way count/weight/connectedness theorem is not a special case of those theorems. value.rationale: The four natural parity classes of complete tripartite bases simultaneously determine the full cardinality weight enumerator and a sharp phase transition (four connected / exactly one / none) rather than an isolated scalar count. The explicit connected claw-free L(K_(1,2m,2m)) family has min degree 4m and 2^(4m-2) ordinary odd-dominating solutions but none connected. This supplies a mathematically motivated unbounded-degree obstruction to connected odd domination and structurally separates existence of many ordinary parity solutions from connected feasibility.
